summary.intent: Add a recipe-based routine system to the ask-soony backend: a recipe format with validation and a compiler that generates sandbox code, plus agent functions and API routes for suggesting, editing, previewing and saving routines.
summary.outcome: Implemented the recipe spec, validation, compiler (with a built-in money/plan brake), and recipe-based suggest/edit/preview/save in routines.py, added tests in tests/test_routines.py, fixed one failing test, and committed the backend.

repo: routines.py holds the recipe format, validation, compiler, agent functions and API routes for routines.
Recipes are compiled into code that runs in a sandbox; the compiler always builds in a money/plan brake.
Routine test runs execute in the sandbox against the real inbox without sending anything (dry run).
The sandbox type checker is strict: recipe lists mixing text and nested dicts made field types ambiguous, so compiled code needs explicit type conversions.
Akshat's newer adapter phrases options as 'Email Supplier: s' rather than using the verifier's option text, so tests matching on option wording must use the adapter phrasing.
workflow: Hand-write recipes and dry-run them against the real inbox to validate the compiler before writing tests.
When a test fails, inspect the failing detail and debug the fixture first; the cause was a wrong test assumption, not a compiler bug.
Run lint and the full suite after adding tests, then commit.

friction: Sandbox type checker rejected the first compiled code because of mixed-type recipe fields, requiring a rerun after making conversions explicit.
One recipe test failed because it assumed the wrong option wording from the adapter.
open_items: A data scout returned five more real cases; one is suited for the routine demo and was to be revisited after the test fix.
The existing seed script was checked after the commit, presumably to be updated for recipe-based routines.
